   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "id": "intro",
   "metadata": {},
   "source": "# Mineral chemistry setup check\n\nUse Windows MATLAB with a registered IPhreeqcCOM server. MRST owns flow and transport; PHREEQC owns local microbial kinetics and chemistry. This deliberately short setup uses four cells and two injection timesteps."
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "code",
   "id": "run-example",
   "metadata": {},
   "source": "startupH2sim\ncomparison = exampleCompositionalBacterial1DPhreeqcMinerals( ...\n    'gridCells', 4, 'maximumFlowSteps', 2);\nstate = comparison(2).states{end};\npH = state.phreeqcPH;\nelementChecks = state.phreeqcElementBalancePass;\n\n% Redraw accepted states without solving again.\nplotPhreeqcMineralComparison(comparison, ...\n    'outputDirectory', fullfile(pwd, 'build', 'example-figures'));",
   "execution_count": null,
   "outputs": []
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "id": "interpret",
   "metadata": {},
   "source": "## Read the plots\n\n![Short mineral comparison](attachment:mineral_comparison.png)\n\nThe original MRST case and PHREEQC cases have different kinetic owners. Their differences are not a pure mineral effect. The original case has no PHREEQC pH. Check the elemental audit and evaluated-cell mask before interpreting chemistry output.\n\n`comparison(k).states` retains the state history. The example uses packed simulation output, allowing accepted results to be replotted.",
